title: Row-Column Hybrid Grouping for Fault-Resilient Multi-Bit Weight Representation on IMC Arrays
problem: Analog IMC systems suffer from stuck-at faults (SAFs) that reduce computational reliability and existing fault-mitigation algorithms (e.g., Fault-Free) impose high compilation overhead. Fault-resilient design of IMC arrays remains computationally expensive and challenging to scale.
motivation: Enabling fault-tolerant in-memory computing is essential for deploying reliable neural accelerators, particularly as IMC arrays scale to larger sizes where faults become more prevalent.
method: The paper proposes row-column hybrid grouping that generalizes column grouping by introducing redundancy across both rows and columns in weight representation. A compiler pipeline reformulates fault-aware weight decomposition as an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) task solved by off-the-shelf solvers. Theoretical insights identify fault patterns with trivial solutions, significantly reducing computation time while maintaining fault tolerance.
key_novelty: 2D redundancy structure (row-column hybrid grouping) combined with ILP-based compilation for fast, scalable fault-aware weight decomposition in IMC arrays.
contributions: Row-column hybrid grouping technique extending conventional column grouping with 2D redundancy structure
ILP-formulated compiler pipeline for fast fault-aware weight decomposition with theoretical optimization
Demonstration of up to 8%p accuracy improvement and 2× energy efficiency gain on CNNs and small LLMs
150× faster compilation compared to existing Fault-Free baselines
limitations: Evaluation limited to relatively small LLMs (not specified which models), and scalability to larger IMC arrays and models may vary with different fault distributions.
